judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's central mathematical claim is refuted by the answer key. It wrote "The open comparisons correctly explain why the outlier changes the mean and range but not the median" and scored mathematical_correctness 4. answer_key.pdf problem 11(b) reads: "Without Devi there are eight values, so the median is halfway between the fourth and fifth: halfway between 5 and 7, which is 6. The median has not moved at all." The eight remaining values are 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10. The fourth is 5 and the fifth is 6, not 7, so the median is 5.5 — it DID move, from 6 down to 5.5. The 11(c) model answer repeats the error ("the median stays at 6 either way") and verify.json's manual desc for problem 11 hard-codes it a third time ("the median stays at 6"), so the marking guidance a teacher would follow is wrong on exactly the point the item exists to teach — the resistance of the median. Everything else the judge says holds: mode 1, median 2, mean 2, range 5, Q1 1, Q3 3, IQR 2, P = 4/11, and for the reading data median 6, mean 8, range 21, mean without Devi 6, Q1 4.5, Q3 9 and IQR 4.5 all reproduce. That does not rescue a 4 on mathematical_correctness for a delivered key that misreads its own sorted list.

strengths_to_preserve: Problem 12 is handled exactly right and is the sheet's strongest item: nine values, the median 6 excluded from both halves, lower half 3, 4, 5, 5 giving Q1 = 4.5 and upper half 7, 8, 10, 24 giving Q3 = 9, so IQR = 4.5 — half-integer quartiles included rather than dodged, and matching the convention the sheet states up front.

The dot-plot misreading is anticipated and machine-checked: problem 3's trap expr (0 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5)/6 = 2.5 is exactly what a student who averages the six axis labels instead of the eleven games computes, and the stem warns "count the dots, not the labels".

Both open items (11c, 12c) carry manual entries whose desc states what earns full credit AND what does not ("do not accept an answer that only says 4.5 is smaller than 21"), and the key repeats that as an explicit marking guide with partial credit bands.

The 1-to-7 ramp is built on one small data set, so the student meets mode, median, mean, range, quartiles, IQR and probability on the SAME eleven games — the measures get compared rather than merely practised.

root_causes.description: The answer key mis-identifies the fifth value of the outlier-removed list, computing the median of 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 as halfway between 5 and 7 instead of between 5 and 6, and then draws the opposite conclusion from the true one.
evidence: answer_key.pdf problem 11(b): "halfway between 5 and 7, which is 6. The median has not moved at all." The correct value is 5.5.
answer_key.pdf problem 11(c) model answer: "the median stays at 6 either way".
verify.json id 11 manual desc: "with her removed the mean drops to 6 and the median stays at 6" — the error is baked into the marking guidance.
The nine-value claims are all correct, so the defect is confined to the eight-value derived set.

root_causes.description: Problem 11(b) is a printed answer slot with no verify entry: id 11 declares a stats mean over the eight-value list and a manual entry, but no median over that same list. A single stats/median entry would have returned 5.5 and made the printed error impossible. The same gap leaves problem 12's Q1 and Q3 slots unverified.
evidence: verify.json id 11 entries: stats mean over [3,4,5,5,6,7,8,10] expecting 6, plus a manual entry. No median entry over that list.
worksheet.pdf problem 11(b): "What happens to the median when Devi is left out?" — an answer slot on the sheet.
worksheet.pdf problem 12(a) prints "Q1 = ___ Q3 = ___ IQR: ___" while verify.json id 12 declares iqr only.
Problem 5 on the same sheet DOES declare q1 and q3 as separate entries, so the pattern was available and simply not applied to the derived data set.

root_causes.description: The seven-page compile against a five-page computed ideal is the batch's largest overshoot and cost the visual_and_print_quality point; page_budget's front-matter charge and its flat +2 slack let it through with no signal.
evidence: python3 scripts/page_budget.py on this verify.json: "12 problems, 99.1cm of content, ideal 5 page(s), accepted range 3-7"; the compiled worksheet.pdf is 7 pages and gate layout-ws PASSED.
Seven of the twelve problems repeat the same dot plot, each charged as a fresh block, so the sheet pays for the figure seven times.
scripts/page_budget.py line 105: SLACK_OVER = 2; line 281: title_block_cm = 2.0 * scale.

improvements.title: Correct problem 11(b): the median of the eight readers without Devi is 5.5, not 6
improvements.proposed_change: Rewrite answer key 11(b) to read: the eight remaining values are 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, so the median is halfway between the fourth (5) and the fifth (6), giving 5.5 — the median drops by half a book while the mean drops by two whole books. Rewrite the 11(c) model answer and verify.json's manual desc to match, and keep the pedagogical point by making it the honest one: the mean falls 8 → 6 and the median 6 → 5.5, so the outlier moves the mean four times as far. The "if Devi had read 240 books" follow-up in the key is correct as written (it is about the nine-value set) and should stay.
improvements.regression_test: Add a stats/median entry over [3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10] to this task's verify.json and re-run scripts/verify.py: it returns 5.5, and tests/check_answer_key.py's per-problem binding then fails the key text asserting 6 for problem 11(b). Both the verifier disagreement and the binding failure are absent today because the entry does not exist.
improvements.expected_impact: A delivered answer key stops teaching a false claim about the median's resistance to outliers — the exact idea problem 11 exists to establish — and the marking guidance a teacher reads stops contradicting the data printed beside it.
improvements.risk: Changing the number changes the sheet's story slightly: the median is no longer perfectly unmoved, so the (c) marking guide has to argue from relative movement rather than from zero movement. That is a better argument, but the prose has to be rewritten carefully rather than patched.

improvements.title: Require one verify entry per printed answer slot, not per problem id
improvements.proposed_change: Extend tests/check_answer_line.py to count the response slots inside each \problem block (\ansblank, \answerline, and the inline "X = ___" runs these sheets use) and fail the build when a problem's slot count exceeds the number of verify entries carrying an expected for that id, naming the uncovered slot. SKILL.md should state the rule as "every blank the student fills is either machine-verified or declared manual". This case is the argument for the rule: the one printed slot on the sheet with no verify entry behind it is the one that is wrong.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture reproducing problem 11: a stem asking for the mean AND the median of a derived subset, with verify.json declaring only the mean. check_answer_line.py must exit non-zero naming the uncovered median slot; adding the median entry makes it pass. Fails today — this task ships that shape with all 22 gates green.
improvements.expected_impact: Directly prevents the class of error that produced this case's wrong answer, and closes the same gap on problem 12's unverified Q1/Q3 slots and on curr-196's Class B quartiles.
improvements.risk: Slot counting from LaTeX is approximate — a stem that lays out a worked table or a units label could be miscounted — so the counter must bind to the shipped answer macros rather than to loose underscores, and authors need a way to declare an intentionally unfilled prompt line.

improvements.title: Charge the directions block and continuation headers in the page budget, and warn when the compiled sheet exceeds its own ideal
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes in scripts/page_budget.py. (1) Replace the flat 2.0cm front matter with a measured charge: when --from-tex is supplied, count the subtitle's wrapped lines and the directions/itemize block before the first \problem and charge their real height; add a per-continuation-page charge for the running header. (2) Keep SLACK_OVER as the failure threshold but have scripts/build.sh print an explicit "pages N > ideal M — trim a stem or drop a problem" warning whenever the compiled count exceeds ideal_pages, so the author sees the overshoot instead of a silent PASS. On a sheet like this one, where the same dot plot is redrawn for seven problems, the warning is what tells the author to group the repeated figure.
improvements.regression_test: In tests/test_page_budget.py add a fixture ws.tex carrying a five-bullet directions block and assert budget(--from-tex) returns an ideal at least 1 greater than the same verify.json with a bare title; and assert build.sh emits the "> ideal" warning for a 7-page compile against ideal 5. Both fail today because the front matter is a constant and no warning exists.
improvements.expected_impact: Sheets stop landing one or two pages above their own budget with a silent PASS; the two cases in this batch that lost a visual_and_print_quality point are both overshoots this warning would have surfaced before delivery.
improvements.risk: Raising ideal_pages also raises max_pages, so a genuinely bloated sheet could slip further before failing; the warning has to be loud enough to compensate, and the existing page-budget fixtures need re-baselining.

case_summary: A well-designed centre-and-spread ramp that walks one eleven-game data set through mode, median, mean, range, quartiles, IQR and probability before switching to a nine-reader set with a genuine outlier, and its quartile work (Q1 4.5, Q3 9, IQR 4.5 on nine values) is careful and correct. It ships a mathematical error anyway. Answer key 11(b) computes the median of the eight readers without Devi as "halfway between 5 and 7, which is 6", but the fourth and fifth of 3, 4, 5, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 are 5 and 6, so the median is 5.5 and it did move. The 11(c) model answer and verify.json's marking guidance repeat the claim, so the false statement is what a teacher grades from — on precisely the idea the item exists to teach. That slot is the only printed answer on the sheet with no verify entry behind it; problem 5 declares q1 and q3 separately, so the pattern existed and was not applied to the derived set. Seven pages against a five-page budget cost the remaining point.
